chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, when the day comes, it says: 'O son of Adam, do good in this day of yours; I will testify for you with it in the Presence of your Lord on the Day of Judgment, for I did not come to you in what has passed, nor will I come to you in what remains.' And when the night comes, it says similar to that.
ai.seo_question: How do the day and night serve as witnesses for human deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) personifies day and night as active witnesses that urge humanity to maximize their righteous deeds, highlighting the transient nature of time as a divine opportunity. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on *muhasaba* (self-accountability), where each passing moment is a chance to accumulate merit that will be presented before Allah on the Day of Judgment. The hadith serves as a spiritual reminder that while the past is gone and the future is uncertain, the present moment is the only arena for earning divine testimony.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Hisham Bin Salim, from one of his companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The day, when it comes, says, ‘O son of Adam<sup>as</sup> work good in this day of yours, I will testify for you with it in the Presence of your Lord<sup>azwj</sup> on the Day of Judgment, for I did not come to you in what is lost (gone) nor will I come to you in what remains (future - as you may not be alive)’. And when the night comes, it says similar to that’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“When the day comes it says, ‘O son of Adam do good deeds this day so I may bear witness to it to testify (in your support) before your Lord on the Day of Judgment. I had not come to you before and will not come to you in future.’ When the night comes it speaks likewise.’”
